To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nucleotide sequence of a new regulatory factor, Sfs1, was determined, and that the protein product of Sfs1 is a new member of the family of transcriptional regulators which have a putative DNA-binding domain.
the sfs1 locus encodes a protein with a putative DNA-binding domain that is involved in CRPMalT-dependent mal gene expression.

we have cloned at least twelve genes from Escherichia Coli which allow strain MK2001, which is deficient in maltose fermentation, to ferment maltose, and we have identified one of these genes, sfs7, as nlp, a homolog of the Mu phage repressor protein Ner, which contains a DNA binding domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a gene which is required for the expression of the maltose regulon in E. coli.
the identification of the sfs gene cluster which has high homologies with the genes of the maltose regulon, and the sfs genes could be a part of a new maltose regulon.
the identification of the genes which are involved in the regulation of maltose metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

sfs7 and sfs1 are the genes which encode the repressor protein and the activator protein for the maltose operon, respectively, although the precise mechanism by which these proteins function in maltose operon regulation remains to be elucidated.
Sfs1 is a new regulatory protein involved in CRP* (cAMP receptor protein)-dependent maltose metabolism.
Sfs1 is involved with the MalT-dependent regulation of the amylomaltose operon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sfs1 and sfs7 are involved in CRP-dependent Mal gene expression, and sfs2 to sfs12 are involved in CRPP-dependent Mal gene expression in E. coli.
sfs1 is a new gene which is involved in CRPMal*-dependent maltose metabolism.
sfs genes are involved in maltose fermentation and that the sfs gene products could be a novel class of transcription factors which are involved in the regulation of the maltose regulon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Sfs1 protein contains a putative helix-turn-helix motif and is involved in CRPl-dependent mal gene expression.
Sfs1 is not involved in the regulation of the maltose regulon, but it is a novel regulator of malEFG genes, and the regulation mechanism is different from that of the maltose system.
Sfs1 is not involved in the regulation of the mal gene cluster but is involved in a different aspect of maltose metabolism.
